title: Dandelion leaf infusion for mild fluid retention
subtitle: The leaf, not the root: a gentle diuretic cup
excerpt: A hot infusion of dried dandelion leaf for mild fluid retention and puffiness. The leaf is a gentler preparation than the root decoction, with a primarily diuretic action rather than the root's stronger bitter-tonic effect. One teaspoon of dried leaf per 200 ml, steeped covered for ten minutes.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), dandelion entry: distinguishes the leaf and root actions, noting the leaf's diuretic properties and traditional use for oedema. BHP (1983) dandelion leaf monograph: dosing reference for dried leaf infusion. EMA HMPC monograph on Taraxaci officinalis herba (2009): diuretic action, safety note on gallstones and allergen note for Asteraceae.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried dandelion leaf stores 12 months in a sealed tin or jar away from light. Prepare each cup fresh.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Prepare fresh for each dose. Do not store the brewed infusion.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation made by pouring just-boiled water over leaves or flowers and steeping them covered, so the volatile oils stay in the cup rather than escaping with the steam.

A herb or substance that increases the flow of urine, traditionally used to reduce mild fluid retention. Unlike pharmaceutical diuretics, dandelion leaf also provides potassium, which is lost through urine.

content.text: Dandelion leaf infusion is a hot cup of dried dandelion leaf steeped in just-boiled water, traditionally used for mild fluid retention and puffiness. This is the leaf preparation, not the root: the leaf is primarily

in action, while the root's main use is as a digestive bitter and liver tonic. The two are different preparations for different purposes. The infusion is pale green-gold, mildly bitter, and smells of damp greenery. One teaspoon of dried leaf per 200 ml, steeped covered for ten minutes, makes a single cup.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

Allergen note: dandelion belongs to the daisy family (Asteraceae). Readers with a known allergy to ragweed, daisies, chamomile, or related plants should use with caution and patch-test before a full therapeutic dose.

Gallstones: dandelion leaf, like the root, stimulates bile flow. This is less pronounced in the leaf than the root, but readers who know they have gallstones should consult a herbalist or their doctor before using this preparation, as stimulating bile flow when stones are present can cause discomfort or worse.

helps the body pass water medication: readers already taking prescribed helps the body pass water medication should consult their prescriber before adding a herbal helps the body pass water. The combination can increase fluid and electrolyte loss beyond what is intended.

Lithium: readers prescribed lithium should consult their prescriber, as helps the body pass water herbs can affect lithium excretion.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine, or a paediatric doctor, before using any herbal preparation in children under twelve.

content.text: Put 1 teaspoon of dried dandelion leaf into a teapot or covered cup.
Pour over 200 ml of just-boiled water and lid immediately.
Steep covered for 10 minutes. The water turns pale greenish-gold.
Strain through a sieve and drink warm.
One cup (200 ml) two to three times a day, between meals. For a short course of up to two weeks. If fluid retention persists, see your doctor to rule out an underlying cause.
Prepare each cup fresh. Dried dandelion leaf stores in a sealed tin or jar, away from light and heat, for up to 12 months.
When not to use this remedy

See a GP for fluid retention that is persistent, getting worse, involves one or both legs becoming notably swollen, or comes alongside breathlessness, chest pain, or a change in heart rate. These patterns need a medical diagnosis.

Do not use if you have known gallstones, or if you are prescribed helps the body pass water medication or lithium, without first consulting your prescriber. Do not use if you have a known Asteraceae allergy. Do not use in children under twelve without specialist paediatric guidance.

items.symptom: Cup tastes very bitter and unpleasant
items.cause: Steeped too long, or used too much herb
items.fix: Keep to 10 minutes and 1 teaspoon. Dandelion leaf is naturally mild-bitter; prolonged steeping pushes it into harsh territory.

items.cause: Dried leaf is old or stored in the light
items.fix: Replace with fresh dried dandelion leaf stored in a sealed container away from direct light.
